image_prompt.text: An old reception counter desk of dark worn wood standing at the centre of the lobby, the one large form the whole room reads from
A clear walkable grain from the arched entrance on the front wall, past the reception counter, through to the exit on the back wall
The composed view in from the arched entrance: cracked tile floor, corner pillars, and the broken chandelier framed against the far wall
Four tall walls of dark weathered grey stone brick closing the lobby in on every side, with no way past them
A tall arched entrance opening in the front wall, framing the lobby so the first thing a player sees is composed
A large rectangular floor of dark cracked stone tiles
A low ceiling of dark decaying panels hanging close overhead
Four tall cracked stone pillars, one standing in each corner of the room
A broken chandelier hanging from the ceiling over the middle of the room
An exit doorway in the back wall, opposite the entrance
A dark, moody palette throughout — deep greys, blacks and dark browns, abandoned and decayed like an old haunted hotel or hospital lobby

layout_placement.text: Players arrive at the arched entrance in the front wall, facing down the lobby toward the reception counter

notes: Stage A outcome None: the prompt describes a place, its materials and its mood — one room, with no game type, objective or mechanic anywhere in it. 'For a horror game' is a theme attached to a room, not Survival's killer or chase, so no genre was invented to escape no-genre.md.

Enclosure set to interior-only: the entire map is one enclosed room. That is the axis value and it carries no pipeline cost — it is not `building-interior`, and there is no outside-to-inside transition, so no P3.
The ceiling and the hanging chandelier are dressing, not overhanging play surfaces, so verticality stays single-surface and the route stays P0.

Preset Explorable Place taken whole — landmark, circulation route and composed vantage all land on things the prompt actually named. Only the enclosure axis was moved off its default, which changes nothing about the route.

The four walls were promoted to `boundary-edge` and the arched entrance to `spawn-area`. The floor, ceiling, corner pillars, chandelier, exit doorway and colour palette matched no option in the loaded file and carry `id: null`.
The colour palette and decayed vibe are filed in image_prompt because the image model is what renders them, even though they are a property of geometry rather than geometry itself.

Cannot be built as layout: the request to expose attributes for fog level, wall darkness and light intensity. That is a Studio-side customisation surface, not geometry or a placed volume — the pipeline should carry it through as tunable attributes on the finished room rather than dropping it.

would have asked: Sounds like an environment showcase built inside one enclosed room — a centrepiece the room reads from, a clear route from the entrance through to the exit, and a composed view in from the arched doorway, all in the dark decayed palette you described. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?

would have asked: Is this the pre-round lobby where players gather before a horror match, or a room inside the haunted building that they pass through? If people congregate here I would add `social-hub` for the open floor; I left it out rather than assume, and it would also make this a round-based game rather than a pure place.

would have asked: The corner pillars and the walls close the room in — do you want anything out on the floor to break sightlines and hide behind (`cover-los`), or should the floor stay open around the counter?
would have asked: Anything else you want in the space?
